title: Alcohol Withdrawal
diagnosis: Moderate alcohol withdrawal — prior delirium tremens history
source: U-Word Psychiatry v02 concepts (Immersa rewrite) — anchor for Uber U12
correct_orders: Seizure precautions / ICU if severe DT risk
should_avoid: Discharge before withdrawal plateau without follow-up

rationale.CIWA-Ar protocol / symptom-triggered ben: Last drink 36 hours ago with tremor and diaphoresis — scale-guided lorazepam or diazepam reduces seizure and DT risk.
rationale.Thiamine / folate / multivitamin (Wernic: Give thiamine before glucose in at-risk drinkers — prevents Wernicke encephalopathy.
rationale.BMP / magnesium / LFTs / ethanol level: Correct hypomagnesemia and assess hepatic injury; low ethanol level confirms withdrawal timing.
rationale.Seizure precautions / ICU if severe DT r: History of prior DT — lower threshold for ICU and continuous monitoring.
rationale.Monitor for delirium tremens: Visual hallucinations today — track autonomic instability, agitation, and fever for DT progression.
rationale.Addiction medicine / psychiatry consult: Link to detox, counseling, and relapse prevention after medical stabilization.
rationale.Safety assessment after intentional rela: Document intent, supports, and safety if withdrawal followed deliberate drinking.
rationale.Fixed-dose benzo without CIWA monitoring: Under- or over-sedation risk — CIWA-triggered dosing is standard.
rationale.Discharge before withdrawal plateau with: High recurrence of seizures/DT if sent home too early without linkage.

hpi: Tom Hayes is a 45-year-old man brought by his partner for shaking, sweating, and "seeing bugs on the wall" since yesterday. His last drink was a pint of whiskey about 36 hours ago — he has tried to quit before and had a seizure and hospital admission for delirium tremens two years ago. He drinks roughly a liter of whiskey daily when actively using. Today he is anxious, tremulous, tachycardic, and oriented but reports visual hallucinations of insects crawling on the curtain. Partner says he drank heavily after losing his job last month and became despondent. No head trauma, no fever, no focal weakness. He wants help quitting but fears "the shakes getting worse like last time."
hpi_narrative:
Tom Hayes is a 45-year-old man brought by his partner for shaking, sweating, and "seeing bugs on the wall" since yesterday. His last drink was a pint of whiskey about 36 hours ago — he has tried to quit before and had a seizure and hospital admission for delirium tremens two years ago. He drinks roughly a liter of whiskey daily when actively using. Today he is anxious, tremulous, tachycardic, and oriented but reports visual hallucinations of insects crawling on the curtain. Partner says he drank heavily after losing his job last month and became despondent. No head trauma, no fever, no focal weakness. He wants help quitting but fears "the shakes getting worse like last time."

Mechanism: GABA receptor downregulation after chronic ethanol exposure produces autonomic hyperactivity 24–72 hours after last drink — tremor, tachycardia, hallucinations; prior DT raises risk of seizures and progression to delirium tremens.

Treatment: CIWA-driven benzodiazepines, thiamine/folate, correct electrolytes, seizure precautions, monitor for DT; addiction consult and safety planning after stabilization.
